rationale: Retain Copia Power as a current Carlyle infrastructure platform and add the signed outbound sale to EQT Infrastructure VII as pending. Carlyle announced Copia as a wholly owned platform in 2021, but no direct source reviewed identifies Carlyle Global Infrastructure Opportunity Fund or another specific Carlyle fund or vehicle, so the unsupported production attribution is removed. Carlyle and EQT announced the sale on July 9, 2026 and described it as subject to customary conditions with an expected closing by year-end; no closing release was found through August 19, 2026. Carlyle therefore remains the current owner until legal closing. Birch Infrastructure's renewable-energy business was combined into Copia, while the individual development projects beneath the platform are not separate manager-level PortCos.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Copia Power is a Carlyle-owned U.S. power and digital infrastructure platform that develops, owns and operates utility-scale solar, battery storage, dispatchable generation, transmission and substation infrastructure, and data-center campuses. Its customers include utilities, public-power entities, hyperscalers, industrial users and other large-load customers. Carlyle launched Copia as a wholly owned platform in 2021 and later combined it with Birch Infrastructure's renewable-energy business. Carlyle and EQT announced a signed agreement on July 9, 2026 for EQT Infrastructure VII to acquire Copia, but the transaction remained subject to customary conditions and no closing was verified through August 19, 2026. Carlyle therefore remains the active owner while the sale is shown separately as pending. Copia's exact legal entity name, the applicable Carlyle fund and vehicle, and the sale consideration and exact legal closing date are not publicly disclosed.
